headline: Anthropic cuts IPO target to $1.4 trillion, lands $26 billion
dek: Seven tech companies will buy shares outside the public offering, per Fortune.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Smaller target, bigger check
body: Anthropic set its IPO valuation at up to $1.4 trillion, below the $2 trillion in earlier reports, per Fortune and The Verge.
In the same filing, seven companies pledged to buy shares outside the public offering (Fortune).

points.t: Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC Partners.
Google and Microsoft are on the list.
Non-voting Class N, in a private placement.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: How much it could raise
body: Adding the IPO and the placement, Fortune calculates up to $90.4 billion.
Business Insider says the deal revives criticism of AI's circular financing.

stat.cap: in shares bought by seven companies (Fortune)

items.t: Banks weigh a higher price, says Fortune.
Dan Ives suggests pricing near $1 trillion (Fortune).

caption.hook: Anthropic cut its IPO target to $1.4 trillion and landed $26 billion from tech giants.
body: Per Fortune and The Verge, the valuation fell from the roughly $2 trillion in earlier reports. Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC Partners pledged to buy $26 billion in non-voting Class N shares in a private placement, per Fortune and Business Insider.

Adding the IPO, Fortune calculates that Anthropic could raise up to $90.4 billion. Business Insider notes the deal revives criticism of circular financing in the AI industry. Per Fortune, citing the Financial Times, the banks are already weighing a price above the filed range.
caption.cta: Is circular financing a risk for AI?
